title: Not All Error Yields to Scale: Where Scaling Stops in Vision-Language Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.01640v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) face a fixed-budget trade-off between processing more visual information for fine-grained perception and using a larger language backbone for complex reasoning. Existing studies do not tell us which combination of backbone size and input resolution to deploy, especially in high-resolution deployments. To address this gap, we propose the Separable Law that describes how VLM performance changes with language backbone size and visual token count. We fit the law to measurements from 26 InternVL and QwenVL models, with language backbone sizes from 1B to 72B, on four high-resolution benchmarks with image sizes from 224 pixels to 8K. We find that the questions responding to scaling can be predicted from the skill they require, while a substantial fraction never responds at all. We also find that the two model families gain similarly from a larger backbone, while their gains from more visual tokens differ sharply.

translated_title: 并非所有误差都能通过规模化消除：视觉语言推理中规模化的止境
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）面临固定预算下的权衡：是处理更多视觉信息以实现细粒度感知，还是使用更大的语言骨干网络以进行复杂推理。现有研究并未告诉我们应部署哪种骨干网络规模与输入分辨率的组合，尤其是在高分辨率部署场景中。为填补这一空白，我们提出“可分离定律”，描述VLM性能如何随语言骨干网络规模和视觉token数量而变化。我们将该定律拟合到26个InternVL和QwenVL模型的测量数据上，这些模型的语言骨干规模从1B到72B，并在四个高分辨率基准测试上进行评估，图像尺寸从224像素到8K。我们发现，对扩展有响应的问题可以根据其所需技能来预测，而相当大一部分问题始终对扩展没有响应。我们还发现，两个模型家族从更大的骨干网络中获得的收益相似，但从更多视觉token中获得的收益却差异显著。
tldr: 该论文提出描述VLM性能随语言骨干规模与视觉token数量变化规律的“可分离定律”，揭示了并非所有错误都能通过规模化消除，且不同模型家族在视觉token扩展上的收益差异显著。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Separable Law describing how VLM performance changes with language backbone size and visual token count, revealing that a substantial fraction of errors never yields to scaling and that model families differ sharply in their gains from more visual tokens.
